dialogues.speaker: Apraksina
dialogues.text: What is it, Bogatov? What are you waiting for?

dialogues.speaker: Bogatov
dialogues.text: Do I... really have to go with you?

dialogues.speaker: Bogatov
dialogues.text: But I'll never be able to return if I take the boat to Nod-Krai with you like that. My father will surely disown me...

dialogues.speaker: Apraksina
dialogues.text: What in the world are you talking about? Things like family name and wealth stopped meaning a thing the very moment we decided to run away together. Or do you still intend to carry those to your grave?

dialogues.speaker: Bogatov
dialogues.text: I... just don't know how we're going to survive without them...

dialogues.speaker: Apraksina
dialogues.text: Goodness me! Just what use are those fangs and claws of yours? Or has time stripped you of the weapons of your ancestors, and left you with nothing but a soft, fuzzy coat?

dialogues.speaker: Apraksina
dialogues.text: You were the one who swore at the opera house that you'd take me to the sea to find freedom. And now you're the one thinking of backing out!?

dialogues.speaker: Bogatov
dialogues.text: Maybe there's another way. Maybe I can still persuade my mother... I just think that we shouldn't be so reckless...

dialogues.speaker: Apraksina
dialogues.text: *Sigh* Maybe I was wrong about you. I thought I could count on you to break me out of the cage. But I guess that was just wishful thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Bogatov
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... Would you hate me if I cannot leave Snezhnaya with you?

dialogues.speaker: Apraksina
dialogues.text: Of course not, Bogatov. I won't have the time to hate you. Even if I have to do it by myself, I will get on that boat and go where I truly wish to go.

dialogues.speaker: Bogatov
dialogues.text: Apraksina... you have always been so much more decisive than I. Honestly, between the two of us, you resemble my great ancestor King Mstislav far more than I ever could. I only wish... I wish I could be even half as courageous as you are...
